# Isolated TX notification observation for the 30 Hz seek failure

This task branch adds a copied-value observer to current maintained driver
538d9fc. It does not fix the retained same-HANDLE seek failure. Native execution
is pending. Original source, PES observations, failures and separate terminal
recovery receipts remain unchanged.

Build the isolated module with `CRYSTALHD_PM_RESEARCH=1
CRYSTALHD_TX_NOTIFY_RESEARCH=1 W=1`. Its explicit version is
`3.10.26-txnotify1`; normal builds omit the observer. Research power limits stay
`pm_research_attempts=0 pm_research_ms=0` for the proposed OFF comparison. No
production default, firmware, input, retry, status or ownership rule changes.
The already-built same-HANDLE PES client and fixed DIL remain separate inputs.

The readonly endpoint `/sys/kernel/debug/crystalhd-tx-notify/trace` reads only
copied host memory. It never opens a device or reads a register/DRAM address.
The store has8192 static module-lifetime records, at most12 values each, a
separate short IRQ-safe lock and explicit dropped/invalid/saturated counters.
It survives device close and has no PM-claim dependency. Record paths allocate
nothing and perform no file I/O. Readout allocates a host snapshot, copies it
under that lock, then formats outside the lock; its file ownership pins the
module. Module exit unregisters the device before removing the endpoint.

Each row records index, monotonic observation time, opaque context identity,
event number, value count and `v0..vN` as hexadecimal DWORDs:

| Event | Values in order |
| --- | --- |
| 1 OPEN | request sequence, channel, metadata address, cleared cache address/size/HostXferSz/flags/sequence |
| 2 advertisement | metadata address, original read status, original address/size/HostXferSz/flags/sequence/channel DWORDs |
| 3 descriptor | selected destination, requested bytes, local flags, descriptor-build status, metadata address, mapped SG count, tail bytes |
| 4 prepare | metadata address, original write DWORD count, write status, written address/size/HostXferSz |
| 5 start | list index, list tag, descriptor physical low/high address, selected destination, requested bytes, metadata address |
| 6 IRQ | original interrupt bits, tag seed, metadata address; observed before TX completion callbacks |
| 7 done | metadata address, sequence-word address, original read status, sequence before, sequence written, original write status, scratch before, scratch written |

Advertisement values are initialized local copies; a failed read does not make
all those words valid device observations. Descriptor records preserve the
actual destination argument and builder result; they are not device-memory
readback. Start records precede the existing void engine call. Done records
follow the existing four sequence/scratch accesses. The sequence read/write
statuses were previously ignored; this diagnostic **still ignores them for
control flow**, retaining their results only for attribution. Read failure can
therefore leave local zero followed by a written1, and write failure can still
be followed by scratch notification; controls must preserve this original
behavior rather than manufacture a repair.

The current TX completion callback precedes firmware sequence notification.
Consequently a successful input ioctl alone does not prove notification,
correct physical destination or firmware consumption. Joining these records
with same-call PES bytes can identify a narrower boundary; it cannot by itself
establish a firmware defect. Record copying and locking add overhead and may
change scheduling. Overflow/incomplete acquisition cannot qualify a complete
history. No historical unstarted metadata addresses are assumed for this run.

Affected verification reuses actual TX admission/descriptor/preparation tests
and adds a small actual notification-function harness for success, failed
read/write and wrap behavior, plus bounded record storage. Device-free tests
and a W=1 module build do not establish native recovery or a release result.

The final affected TX-admission run passes11,548 checks in each normal and
sanitized configuration. Actual notification controls cover six cases plus
the8192-slot bound, invalid/saturated counters and default no-evaluation path;
normal and ASan/UBSan runs pass with the observer absent and present. W=1
module build02 passes with the declared version. The first focused sanitizer
attempt exposed the pre-existing null-member-address expression for SeqNum;
its original failure remains, and a separate `offsetof` correction computes
exactly the same16-byte offset with defined C behavior. This is not evidence
that the native seek stall was repaired.
